articles.title: Middleton Shopping Centre Receives Approval for New Signage and Improvements
articles.excerpt: Middleton Shopping Centre has been granted permission for enhancements, including new signage, as part of a broader investment plan to improve the site.
articles.content_html:
Middleton Shopping Centre has received approval from Rochdale Council to proceed with the next phase of its redevelopment, which includes the addition of new signage. The centre, which was sold to AG Retail, a subsidiary of the Adhan Group, in June 2025, aims to enhance its visual appeal and functionality for shoppers.

The approved plans involve creating two signage zones on the side of the centre facing the bus station. These zones will feature powder-coated aluminium panels finished in grey, designed to match the existing building's elevation. This initiative is part of a larger investment programme aimed at revitalising the shopping centre, which offers 324,078 square feet of retail space across 87 units, along with a 430-space multi-storey car park.

In addition to the signage, planning permission was granted on July 4, 2025, for the installation of eight short-stay parking bays and two disabled parking bays to the south of the shopping centre. Retailers such as Boyes and Mother Hubbard are currently fitting out new units within the centre, signalling a positive shift in the retail landscape of Middleton.

The improvements at Middleton Shopping Centre are expected to enhance the shopping experience for local residents and visitors, potentially increasing foot traffic and supporting local businesses. Further developments will be monitored as the centre continues its transformation.

articles.title: Rochdale AFC Signs Kane Taylor on Loan from Birmingham City
articles.excerpt: Rochdale have secured the loan signing of Kane Taylor from Aston Villa, with the 21-year-old midfielder joining the club until January 2027.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Football Club has announced the signing of midfielder Kane Taylor from Aston Villa on loan until January 2027. The 21-year-old player joins Rochdale after a loan spell at Oldham Athletic last season, where he made 16 appearances and scored two goals, helping the team finish 10th in League Two.

Despite not yet making his senior debut for Aston Villa, Taylor has shown promise, scoring for the Villa Under-21s in an EFL Trophy match against Wigan earlier this week. His experience in League Two is expected to bolster Rochdale's midfield options as they aim for a successful season.

Rochdale manager Ian Watson expressed his delight at securing Taylor's services, stating, "He brings a lot of athleticism and quality to the team, alongside experience in League Two." Watson's comments highlight the club's focus on enhancing their squad ahead of the upcoming fixtures.

The addition of Taylor is likely to provide a boost to Rochdale's performance as they prepare for their next match. Fans will be eager to see how the young midfielder integrates into the team and contributes to their campaign.

articles.title: Tram Services Disrupted Due to Failed Tram at Trafford Bar
articles.excerpt: A failed tram at Trafford Bar has caused significant disruption to services across Greater Manchester, including routes to Rochdale Town Centre. Ticket acceptance is in place on various bus services.
articles.content_html:
A failed tram at Trafford Bar has led to the suspension of tram services between Cornbrook and Trafford Bar as of 3:54pm on Friday, 21 August 2026. This disruption affects several lines, including those connecting Altrincham to Bury, Manchester Airport to Victoria, East Didsbury to Rochdale Town Centre, and Altrincham to Piccadilly/Etihad Campus.

Passengers travelling to and from Rochdale Town Centre should be aware that services are currently not operating due to the incident. Airport services are still running to Firswood, while East Didsbury services are also operating to Firswood. Ticket acceptance is in place on multiple bus routes, including the 23, 25, 41, 43, 85a, 101, 103, 248, 249, and 368, to accommodate affected passengers.

Altrincham services are operating to Old Trafford, with ticket acceptance on routes such as the 11, 15, 245, and 250. Additionally, services from the Trafford Centre are running to Cornbrook, with ticket acceptance on routes including the 30, 150, and 253.

Passengers are advised to check for updates and plan their journeys accordingly as the situation develops. Further information can be found on the Bee Network travel alerts page.

articles.title: Track Renewal Works on Rochdale Line Affecting Tram Services Until 28 August
articles.excerpt: From 15 to 28 August, tram services on the Rochdale line will be disrupted due to track renewal works, with a bus replacement service in operation.
articles.content_html:
Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has announced that track renewal works will take place on the Rochdale line from Saturday 15 August until Friday 28 August. During this period, tram services will be disrupted, and a bus replacement service will operate between the affected stops.

Passengers are advised to plan their journeys accordingly, as the bus replacement service will help maintain connectivity during the works. Further details regarding the specific stops affected can be found on the TfGM travel alerts page.

In addition to the track works, essential improvement works are also scheduled at Prestwich Metrolink stop until 12 October. Tram services will not be affected at this stop, but there will be an increased presence of staff to assist passengers.

Currently, the lifts at Failsworth and Etihad Campus tram stops are out of service, meaning there is no step-free access at these locations. Passengers needing assistance should contact the Metrolink customer service centre at 0161 244 1000 for journey planning support.
